reason: H0 reaches vertex encoding through fuzzRoundtrip, but it supplies unstructured fuzzer bytes directly as vertex records and does not deliberately construct repeated or constant per-component vertex streams. In encodeVertexBlock, such streams are what produce an all-zero zigzag8 delta group, allowing encodeBytesGroupZero to select the new bits[0] == 0 mode. That mode has distinct measurement and emission behavior—encodeBytesGroupMeasure returns zero bytes and encodeBytesGroup advances no output—so it is a fuzz-worthy input semantic not reliably exercised by H0.
evidence: encodeVertexBlock computes buffer[i] = zigzag8(vertex_data[vertex_offset] - p), so identical consecutive values for a component create zero deltas.
kBitsV0 is changed to {0, 2, 4, 8}, introducing a zero-bit candidate passed to encodeBytes.
encodeBytesGroupMeasure handles bits == 0 by requiring encodeBytesGroupZero(buffer) and returning 0 only for an all-zero group.
encodeBytesGroup handles bits == 0 by returning data without emitting payload bytes.
fuzzRoundtrip passes data directly to meshopt_encodeVertexBuffer and contains no construction of repeated vertices or constant component lanes.
recommended_action: Add targeted roundtrip cases that build vertex buffers with at least one complete kByteGroupSize delta group of identical values, including all-zero vertices and repeated nonzero vertices, across the exercised strides and across vertex-block/group boundaries; retain the existing arbitrary-stream decoder calls.
